blockMcqs.question: What is the hardest part of designing a movie booking system?
options: Preventing two users from booking the same seat
blockMcqs.explanation: Browsing and listing are straightforward CRUD; the concurrency problem of double-booking under simultaneous requests is what makes this an LLD-worthy problem.

blockMcqs.question: Why is 'check seat status, then update it' unsafe?
options: It is slower than a single query
It is a check-then-act race condition
blockMcqs.explanation: Two separate steps (read then write) let two concurrent requests both pass the check before either writes, producing a double-booking.

blockMcqs.question: What does the LOCKED SeatStatus represent?
options: The seat is temporarily held during checkout
The seat was cancelled by the user
The seat does not exist on this screen
blockMcqs.explanation: LOCKED is a short-lived state between AVAILABLE and BOOKED, held only while a user completes payment.

blockMcqs.question: Why not mark a seat BOOKED before payment completes?
options: An abandoned checkout would permanently block the seat
It violates the Show entity design
blockMcqs.explanation: If BOOKED were set pre-payment, a user who never pays would permanently strand that seat as unavailable to everyone else.

blockMcqs.question: Why does lockSeats use a rollback if one seat fails to lock?
options: To log an error for analytics
So a partial multi-seat lock does not strand other seats
Because Redis requires transactions for all writes
blockMcqs.explanation: Without rollback, a failed multi-seat request could leave some seats locked by a user who ultimately gets no booking, blocking those seats needlessly.

blockMcqs.question: Which locking style fits a seat with heavy contention?
blockMcqs.explanation: Pessimistic locking fails fast for high-contention seats instead of letting many users start payment only to have most fail on write.

blockMcqs.question: In optimistic locking, how is a conflicting write detected?
blockMcqs.explanation: Optimistic locking lets reads happen freely and rejects a write if the record's version changed since it was read.

blockMcqs.question: Why can't a DB transaction alone solve seat locking?
options: It can't hold a lock across a minutes-long payment gap
Transactions are deprecated in modern databases
Transactions only work with NoSQL stores
blockMcqs.explanation: Holding a DB row lock for the duration of a payment flow would stall other queries and not survive a restart, so the lock needs its own TTL outside the transaction.
